summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation, multiple strokes, tracheostomy, ileostomy, diabetes, and chronic indwelling urinary catheter was admitted from a nursing home for fever and milky urine, concerning for urinary tract infection. He was found to have leukocytosis and pyuria, with urine culture growing Proteus mirabilis. A complication arose when the Foley catheter balloon inflated in the urethra, requiring replacement by urology. He received a 7-day course of intravenous Zosyn, with resolution of fever and infection markers. A concurrent pulmonary infiltrate was noted on chest imaging, but given lack of fever and improving secretions, it was attributed to aspiration pneumonitis rather than pneumonia, and antibiotics for lung coverage were discontinued. He had transient tracheostomy site bleeding that resolved spontaneously. His atrial fibrillation was managed with warfarin, diabetes with increased Lantus insulin, and other comorbidities remained stable. He was discharged to extended care with follow-up recommended in urology for long-term bladder management.
problems: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter
Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food or vomitus
Proteus (mirabilis) (morganii) infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
Urinary catheterization as the cause of abnormal reaction of patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of procedure
Late effects of cerebrovascular disease, aphasia
Other acquired deformities of ankle and foot
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
